name: DG Granule
description: This is a canonical principal cell of the main hippocampal circuit.

name: DG Semilunar Granule
description: This is the only name in the cited literature.

name: DG Mossy
description: This is a canonical secondary cell of the dentate gyrus circuitry and is the name most often cited in the literature.

name: DG Axo-axonic
description: The phrase "chandelier cell" has fallen out of use. DG distinguishes these cells from axo-axonic cells in other subregions.

name: DG Axo-axonic GRALDEN*
description: The phrase "chandelier cell" has fallen out of use. This variant of the standard Axo-axonic has "GRAnular Layer DENdrites." DG distinguishes these cells from axo-axonic cells in other subregions.

name: DG Basket
description: This name omits any descriptive adjectives because not all of the subtypes are clearly known to be PV+. DG distinguishes these cells from basket cells in other subregions.

name: DG Basket CCK+
description: These cells are known to be CCK+. DG distinguishes these cells from basket CCK+ cells in other subregions. "CCK+" was selected as being more compact than "CCK-positive" or "cholecystokinin-positive."

name: DG Interneuron Specific COLTAR*
description: This is a new name derived from the interneuron specificity and is in the vein of HICAP, MOPP, and HIPP that stands for "COLlateral-TARgeting."

name: DG HICAP
description: This name best captures the essence of this mixture of less common and less formal cited names that stands for "HIlar Commissural-Associational Pathway-related."

name: DG Interneuron Specific IMOT*
description: This is a new name derived from the interneuron specificity and the morphological patterning that matches IMOT (Inner MOlecular layer-Targeting) cells.

name: DG Interneuron Specific HIMOLD*
description: This is a new name derived from the interneuron specificity and is in the vein of HICAP, MOPP, and HIPP that stands for "HIlus and MOlecular Layer Dendrites."

name: DG HIPP
description: This name best captures the essence of this mixture of less common and less formal cited names that stands for "HIlar Perforant Path-associated."

name: DG Interneuron Specific HIPRO*
description: This is a new name derived from the interneuron specificity and is in the vein of HICAP, MOPP, and HIPP that stands for "HIlus PROjecting."

name: DG HIPROM
description: This is a new name derived from the cited descriptor in the vein of HICAP, MOPP, and HIPP that stands for "Hilar Interneuron with PRojections to the Outer Molecular layer."

name: DG MOLAX
description: This acronym, which stands for "MOlecular Layer AXons," is cited in the literature to describe a variant of the DG TML type with axons only in SM.

name: DG Total Molecular Layer
description: This is the simplest of the names in the cited literature.

name: DG MOPP
description: This name best captures the essence of this mixture of cited types and stands for "MOlecular layer Perforant Path-associated."

name: DG Neurogliaform
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. DG distinguishes these cells from neurogliaform cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 Pyramidal
description: This is a canonical principal cell of the main hippocampal circuit. CA3 distinguishes these cells from pyramidal cells in other subregions.

name: CA3c Pyramidal
description: The partition modifier distinguishes these cells from the canonical CA3 Pyramidal cells, because of the lack of SLM in CA3c. CA3 distinguishes these cells from pyramidal cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 Granule
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. CA3 distinguishes these cells from the canonical DG granule cells.

name: CA3 Axo-axonic
description: The phrase "chandelier cell" has fallen out of use. CA3 distinguishes these cells from axo-axonic cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 Horizontal Axo-axonic
description: This straightforward name derives from the more common name in the cited literature and is the CA3 variant of the literature-based CA1 Horizontal Axo-Axonic.

name: CA3 Basket
description: This name omits any descriptive adjectives because not all of the subtypes are clearly known to be PV+. CA3 distinguishes these cells from basket cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 Basket CCK+
description: These cells are known to be CCK+. CA3 distinguishes these cells from basket CCK+ cells in other subregions. "CCK+" was selected as being more compact than "CCK-positive" or "cholecystokinin-positive."

name: CA3 Bistratified
description: This is the most well-known name in the cited literature, which is a variant of the more well known CA1 Bistratified. CA3 distinguishes these cells from bistratified cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 Ivy
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. CA3 distinguishes these cells from ivy cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 Lucidum-Radiatum
description: This name describes the axons and dendrites in both SR and SL and borrows from the cited names.

name: CA3 Mossy Fiber-Associated
description: This is the canonical mossy fiber-associated cell, and is the only cited name.

name: CA3 Mossy Fiber-Associated ORDEN
description: This is a variant of the canonical MFA that has "ORiens DENdrites."

name: CA3 O-LM
description: This is the canonical CA3 variant of the canonical CA1 O-LM cell. This is the only name in the cited literature. O-LM stands for "Oriens (dendrites) - Lacunosum-Moleculare (axons)."

name: CA3 Interneuron Specific Oriens
description: This cell is verified to preferentially target non-principal cells. Although more politically loaded, the phrase "interneuron specific" is more compact than "non-principal cell-specific" and is more commonly found in the cited literature.  "Oriens" describes the lcoation of the soma and axons. CA3 distinguishes these cells from interneuron specific cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 Interneuron Specific Quad
description: This cell is verified to preferentially target non-principal cells. Although more politically loaded, the phrase "interneuron specific" is more compact than "non-principal cell-specific" and is more commonly found in the cited literature.  "Quad" describes the lcoations of the axons and dendrites in four layers. CA3 distinguishes these cells from interneuron specific cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 QuadD-LM
description: This is a variant of the CA3 O-LM that has dendrites in four layers. CA3 distinguishes these cells from O-LM cells in other subregions.

name: CA3 Radiatum
description: This simple and compact name captures the presence of axons and dendrites all in SR. CA3 distinguishes these cells from R cells in other subregions.

name: CA2 Pyramidal
description: CA2 distinguishes these cells from pyramidal cells in other subregions.

name: CA2 Basket
description: Although the cells are known to be PV+, this is omitted to match better the "PV+" basket cell names in other subregions. This is the canonical CA2 basket cell compared to the non-projecting variant. CA2 distinguishes these cells from basket cells in other subregions.

name: CA2 Wide-Arbor Basket
description: This name is derived from the cited name, but sounds better to the ear when the modfiers precede the core name. CA2 distinguishes these cells from basket cells in other subregions.

name: CA2 Bistratified
description: The is the only name in the cited literature. This cell has the essence of the CA1 and CA3 bistratified cells in terms of marker expression.

name: CA2 SP-SR
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. SP-SR stands for "Stratum Pyramidale (somata) - Stratum Radiatum (axons)."

name: CA1 Pyramidal
description: This is a canonical principal cell of the main hippocampal circuit. CA1 distinguishes these cells from pyramidal cells in other subregions.

name: CA1 Cajal-Retzius
description: This is the only name in the cited literature.

name: CA1 Axo-axonic
description: The phrase "chandelier cell" has fallen out of use. CA1 distinguishes these cells from axo-axonic cells in other subregions.

name: CA1 Horizontal Axo-axonic
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. CA1 distinguishes these cells from horizontal axo-axonic cells in other subregions.

name: CA1 Back-Projection
description: This is a canonical Klausberger and Somogyi name, is one in the cited literature. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Basket

name: CA1 Horizontal Basket

name: CA1 Basket CCK+
description: These cells are known to be CCK+. CA1 distinguishes these cells from basket CCK+ cells in other subregions. "CCK+" was selected as being more compact than "CCK-positive" or "cholecystokinin-positive."

name: CA1 Bistratified
description: This is a canonical Klausberger and Somogyi name and is the main one in the cited literature. CA1 distinguishes these cells from bistratified cells in other subregions.

name: CA1 Hippocampo-subicular Projecting ENK+
description: The name borrows from one of the cited descriptors in the literature that describes the projecting nature of the cell and its enkephalin-positivity. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Ivy
description: This is the canonical CA1 ivy cell. CA1 distinguishes these cells from ivy cells in other subregions.

name: CA1 Interneuron Specific LM-R
description: This cell is verified to preferentially target non-principal cells. Although more politically loaded, the phrase "interneuron specific" is more compact than "non-principal cell-specific" and is more commonly found in the cited literature. This name is a variant of "O-LM" since the dendrites are in SLM and the axons project to SR. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Interneuron Specific LMO-O
description: This cell is verified to preferentially target non-principal cells. Although more politically loaded, the phrase "interneuron specific" is more compact than "non-principal cell-specific" and is more commonly found in the cited literature. The modifier is a variant of "O-LM" because the dendrites are in SLM and SO and the axons project to SO. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 LMR
description: This name describes the multilayered axons and dendrites that occupy both occupy SLM and SR. There are no hyphens to avoid any confusion with "O-LM"-like names. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Interneuron Specific LMR-O*

name: CA1 Neurogliaform
description: This is the only name in the cited literature and is the canonical CA1 neurogliaform cell. CA1 distinguishes these cells from neurogliaform cells in other subregions.

name: CA1 Neurogliaform Projecting
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. The modifier distinguishes this type from the non-projecting CA1 Neurogliaform. CA1 distinguishes these cells from neurogliaform cells in other subregions.

name: CA1 O-LM
description: This is a canonical CA1 interneuron. CA1 distinguishes these cells from O-LM cells in other subregions. O-LM stands for "Oriens (dendrites) - Lacunosum-Moleculare (axons)."

name: CA1 O-LMR
description: The "R" modifies the only name in the cited literature and distinguishes this cell from the canonical CA1 O-LM cell and from the variant with a recurrent axon in SO. SLM comes before SR in HC ordering of the layers. CA1 distinguishes these cells from O-LM cells in other subregions. O-LMR stands for "Oriens (dendrites) - Lacunosum-Moleculare Radiatum (axons)."

name: CA1 Interneuron Specific O-R
description: This cell is verified to preferentially target non-principal cells. This name is a variant of "O-LM" since the soma and dendrites are in SO and the axons project to SR. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Interneuron Specific O-Targeting QuadD

The modifiers describe the axons that project to SO and the dendrites that are found in four layers. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Oriens/Alveus
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Oriens-Bistratified
description: This name appears most often in the cited literature and fits better than the O-R name that invokes an ambiguous O-LM-type name. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Perforant Path-Associated
description: This is a canonical Klausberger and Somogyi name that is the most well known in the cited literature. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Perforant Path-Associated QuadD
description: This name is the most well known in the cited literature. The modifier describes the dendrites that invade four layers and distinguishes these cells from the canonical perforant path-associated cells.

name: CA1 Quadrilaminar
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Interneuron Specific R-O
description: This cell is verified to preferentially target non-principal cells. name: CA1 R-Receiving Apical-Targeting

name: CA1 Radiatum
description: This simple and compact name captures the presence of axons and dendrites all in SR. CA1 distinguishes these cells from R cells in other subregions.

name: CA1 Interneuron Specific RO-O

name: CA1 Schaffer Collateral-Associated
description: This is a canonical Klausberger and Somogyi name that does not misuse "trilaminar" and is more well-known than "apical dendrite-innervating."

name: CA1 Schaffer Collateral-Receiving R-Targeting
description: The name is derived from one of the more prominent of the cited names and also describes the axons that project to SR.

name: CA1 SO-SO
description: This is one of the cited names from a prominent lab. CA1 distinguishes these cells from SO-SO cells in other subregions. SO-SO stands for "Stratum Oriens (dendrites) - Stratum Oriens (axons)."

name: CA1 Trilaminar
description: This is the canonical Somogyi cell type. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: CA1 Radial Trilaminar
description: This is the most frequently cited name and the modifier distinguishes it from the canonical CA1 Trilaminar. CA1 clarifies the subregion of origin, since the name is otherwise generic.

name: Sub CA1-Projecting Pyramidal
description: This is the only name in the cited literature. The modifer distinguishes it from the EC-targeting variant. Sub distinguishes these cells from pyramidal cells in other subregions.

name: Sub Axo-axonic
description: The phrase "chandelier cell" has fallen out of use. Sub distinguishes these cells from axo-axonic cells in other subregions.

name: EC LI-II Pyramidal-Fan

name: EC MEC LII Oblique Pyramidal

name: EC MEC LII Stellate

name: EC MEC LII-III Pyramidal-Multiform

name: EC LII-III Pyramidal-Tripolar

name: EC MEC LIII Superficial Multipolar Interneuron
description: All sources indicate medial localization of the morphology. Superficial distinguishes these cells from other multipolared interneurons. Multipolar is a descriptor in the cited literature and has the flavor of the standard EC naming scheme.

name: EC MEC LIII Superficial Trilayered Interneuron
